sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State.
3. On the basis of complaint dated 26.06.2023 lodged by Heena Parveen D/o Nazeer Saheb, aged about 24 years, FIR in Crime No.52/2023 was registered against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
In the complaint it is averred that, the complainant was studying MBA and she got acquainted with the petitioner through instagram, about one and half months prior to she lodging complaint.
They had exchanged messages and also used to speak over the phone.
It is averred in the complaint that, they were in love with each other.
The petitioner allegedly got transferred a sum of Rs.20,000/- from the brother-in-law of the complainant on 25.05.2023.
The petitioner invited the complainant to Poonja Internatinal hotel, Hampanakatte and took the complainant to Room No.515.
In NC: 2023:KHC:33852 the said hotel, the petitioner had food along with the complainant and thereafter, in spite of complainant's refusal, the petitioner allegedly had sex with her.
She has further stated that for about 20 days she had gone to the said hotel.
On 27.05.2023, the petitioner allegedly demanded money from the complainant and accordingly, she had paid a sum of Rs.10,000/- to him.
The petitioner continued demanding money from the complainant and he was also allegedly threatening her.
The complainant has further stated that the petitioner was married man and this was not disclosed to her and he had cheated her.
Accordingly, she had approached the police on 26.06.2023.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner was arrested on 27.06.2023.

The bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C, filed by the petitioner before the court of VI Addl.
District & Sessions Judge, D.K, Mangaluru in Crl.Misc.No.660/2023 was dismissed on 18.08.2023.

VI Addl.

sentences.text: It is under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this court.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that even if the allegation in the complaint is presumed to be true, NC: 2023:KHC:33852 offence under Section 376 of IPC cannot be made against the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State has opposed the bail application.
6. On perusal of the complaint averments it is seen that, the complainant had got acquainted with the petitioner through Instagram and thereafter they were in touch with each other.
It is also alleged in the complaint that they were in love with each other.
Thereafter, as per the request of the petitioner the complainant had gone to Poonja international hotel on 25.05. 2023 and on the said date, the petitioner had sex with the complainant.
Even thereafter for about 20 days, the complainant had gone to the said hotel and stayed with the petitioner in the hotel room.
The allegation in the complaint is that, the petitioner had promised to marry the complainant and thereafter backed out.
It is further stated that the petitioner was already married and the said fact was suppressed by the petitioner.

However, the fact remains that the complainant is a major aged about 24 years and the allegation against the petitioner is that he had sex with her promising to marry her.
NC: 2023:KHC:33852
Considering the nature of allegation in the complaint serious doubt arises whether the offence punishable under section 376 of IPC would get attracted against the petitioner.
The same is subject matter of trial.
The petitioner is in custody since 27.06.2023.
Major portion of the investigation is complete.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered affirmatively.
In view of the above, the petition is allowed.
